```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false

# Load package in dev mode or installed
tryCatch(
  pkgload::load_all(quiet = TRUE),
  error = function(e) {
    tryCatch(library(acd), error = function(e2) NULL)
  }
)

if (!exists("ADDRESSES_SNAPSHOT_DATE")) ADDRESSES_SNAPSHOT_DATE <- "2026-05-02"
if (!exists("SNAPSHOT_DATE"))           SNAPSHOT_DATE           <- "2026-05-01"
if (!exists("REMOTE_BASE_URL"))         REMOTE_BASE_URL         <- "https://johngavin.github.io/acd_area_climate_design/data"

# Load addresses for inline summary stats only (not passed to JS)
addr_local <- load_acd_data("addresses", source = "local")

n_addresses      <- nrow(addr_local)
n_acd_codes      <- length(unique(addr_local$ACD))
addr_parquet_url <- paste0(REMOTE_BASE_URL, "/addresses_", ADDRESSES_SNAPSHOT_DATE, ".parquet")
```

```{=html}
<!-- ── Toolbar JS ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── -->
<script>
(function() {
  // ── Constants ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  const LS_LANG      = "acd-upload-lang";
  const LS_FONT      = "acd-upload-font-size";
  const LS_DARK      = "acd-upload-dark-mode";
  const FONT_MIN     = 12;
  const FONT_MAX     = 22;
  const FONT_STEP    = 1;
  const FONT_DEFAULT = 17;  // 1.15em equivalent at base 16px → ~18.4; use 17 as round default

  // ── Helpers ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  function applyLang(lang) {
    document.body.setAttribute("lang", lang);
    const btn = document.getElementById("lang-btn");
    if (btn) {
      btn.textContent = lang === "de" ? "🌐 EN" : "🌐 DE";
      btn.setAttribute("aria-label",
        lang === "de" ? "Switch to English" : "Auf Deutsch wechseln");
      btn.setAttribute("title",
        lang === "de" ? "Switch to English" : "Auf Deutsch wechseln");
    }
    // Swap data-en / data-de textContent on interactive elements (buttons, th, labels)
    document.querySelectorAll("[data-en][data-de]").forEach(el => {
      el.textContent = el.getAttribute("data-" + lang);
    });
  }

  function applyFont(px) {
    document.documentElement.style.setProperty("--upload-font-size", px + "px");
  }

  function applyDark(on) {
    document.body.classList.toggle("dark-mode", on);
    const btn = document.getElementById("dark-btn");
    if (btn) btn.textContent = on ? "☀️" : "🌙";
  }

  // ── First-visit defaults ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
  function detectLang() {
    const saved = localStorage.getItem(LS_LANG);
    if (saved) return saved;
    return (navigator.language || "").startsWith("de") ? "de" : "en";
  }

  function detectDark() {
    const saved = localStorage.getItem(LS_DARK);
    if (saved !== null) return saved === "1";
    return window.matchMedia &&
           window.matchMedia("(prefers-color-scheme: dark)").matches;
  }

  function detectFont() {
    const saved = parseInt(localStorage.getItem(LS_FONT), 10);
    return (saved >= FONT_MIN && saved <= FONT_MAX) ? saved : FONT_DEFAULT;
  }

  // ── Init ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  let currentLang = detectLang();
  let currentFont = detectFont();
  let currentDark = detectDark();

  applyLang(currentLang);
  applyFont(currentFont);
  applyDark(currentDark);

  // ── Button wiring (defer until DOM ready) ─────────────────────────────────
  document.addEventListener("DOMContentLoaded", function() {
    applyLang(currentLang);
    applyFont(currentFont);
    applyDark(currentDark);

    document.getElementById("lang-btn").addEventListener("click", function() {
      currentLang = currentLang === "en" ? "de" : "en";
      localStorage.setItem(LS_LANG, currentLang);
      applyLang(currentLang);
    });

    document.getElementById("font-up-btn").addEventListener("click", function() {
      currentFont = Math.min(FONT_MAX, currentFont + FONT_STEP);
      localStorage.setItem(LS_FONT, currentFont);
      applyFont(currentFont);
    });

    document.getElementById("font-down-btn").addEventListener("click", function() {
      currentFont = Math.max(FONT_MIN, currentFont - FONT_STEP);
      localStorage.setItem(LS_FONT, currentFont);
      applyFont(currentFont);
    });

    document.getElementById("dark-btn").addEventListener("click", function() {
      currentDark = !currentDark;
      localStorage.setItem(LS_DARK, currentDark ? "1" : "0");
      applyDark(currentDark);
    });
  });
})();
</script>
```

## Quick guide

::: {data-lang="en"}
Upload an Excel (`.xlsx`) or CSV file with **at least three columns**: postcode
(`PLZ`), street name, and house number. The lookup runs entirely in your browser
using [DuckDB-Wasm](https://duckdb.org/docs/api/wasm/overview.html) — your file
never leaves your device.
:::

::: {data-lang="de"}
Laden Sie eine Excel- (`.xlsx`-) oder CSV-Datei mit **mindestens drei Spalten** hoch:
Postleitzahl (`PLZ`), Straßenname und Hausnummer. Die Suche läuft vollständig in Ihrem
Browser via [DuckDB-Wasm](https://duckdb.org/docs/api/wasm/overview.html) — Ihre Datei
verlässt Ihr Gerät nicht.
:::

::: {data-lang="en"}
**Example values:** postcode `1210`, street `Achengasse`, house number `3`
→ ACD code `070268`, SCD `00012`.

**Coverage:** `r format(n_addresses, big.mark=",")` registered address points,
`r format(n_acd_codes, big.mark=",")` unique ACD codes.
Source: [Vienna Open Government Data WFS](https://www.data.gv.at/katalog/dataset/stadt-wien_adressenwien)
([`ogdwien:ADRESSENOGD`](https://data.wien.gv.at/daten/geo?service=WFS&request=DescribeFeatureType&typeNames=ogdwien:ADRESSENOGD)),
snapshot `r ADDRESSES_SNAPSHOT_DATE`.

**Privacy:** addresses you upload are processed locally in your browser
via [DuckDB-Wasm](https://duckdb.org/docs/api/wasm/overview.html). They are never sent to any server.
:::

::: {data-lang="de"}
**Beispielwerte:** PLZ `1210`, Straße `Achengasse`, Hausnummer `3`
→ ACD-Code `070268`, SCD `00012`.

**Abdeckung:** `r format(n_addresses, big.mark=".")` registrierte Adresspunkte,
`r format(n_acd_codes, big.mark=".")` eindeutige ACD-Codes.
Quelle: [Wien Open Government Data WFS](https://www.data.gv.at/katalog/dataset/stadt-wien_adressenwien)
([`ogdwien:ADRESSENOGD`](https://data.wien.gv.at/daten/geo?service=WFS&request=DescribeFeatureType&typeNames=ogdwien:ADRESSENOGD)),
Stand `r ADDRESSES_SNAPSHOT_DATE`.

**Datenschutz:** Die hochgeladenen Adressen werden lokal in Ihrem Browser verarbeitet
via [DuckDB-Wasm](https://duckdb.org/docs/api/wasm/overview.html). Es werden keine Daten an einen Server übertragen.
:::

:::

## How it works {.panel-tabset}

### Algorithm / Algorithmus

::: {data-lang="en"}
This page does **not** use the project's spatial join or building-footprint
layer. It is a direct address-table lookup against
[`ogdwien:ADRESSENOGD`](https://data.wien.gv.at/daten/geo?service=WFS&request=DescribeFeatureType&typeNames=ogdwien:ADRESSENOGD)
(`r format(n_addresses, big.mark=",")` registered address points), running in
[DuckDB-Wasm](https://duckdb.org/docs/api/wasm/overview.html) entirely in your
browser. See the [Methodology page](methodology.qmd) for the dashboard's
spatial pipeline (different layers, different question).

The join uses three normalised keys:

- **PLZ** — four-digit postcode (cast to `VARCHAR`)
- **Street name** — `LOWER(TRIM(name_str))` matched against the user column
- **House number** — `LOWER(TRIM(name_onr))` matched against the user column

Schrebergärten / garden-plot addresses with a `/` in the street or `Parz` in
the house-number column are split into two lookup attempts automatically.

### What this page does NOT do

- ❌ It does not run the `R/join_buildings_zones.R` spatial join
- ❌ It does not return `confidence_tier` (A–E distance-based labels)
- ❌ It does not return `zone_id` or `nearest_zone_dist_m` for matched buildings
- ❌ It does not consult the `GEBAEUDEINFOOGD` building-footprint layer

Spatial enrichment of matched rows with these fields is tracked as a follow-up
in [issue #42](https://github.com/JohnGavin/acd_area_climate_design/issues/42).

**Match quality legend:**

| Value | Meaning |
|-------|---------|
| `exact` | All three keys matched exactly after normalisation |
| `fuzzy_nearest_house` | PLZ + street matched; nearest existing house number used (distance shown in `house_distance` column) |
| `split_both` | Composite `A/B` street — both halves resolved to an ACD (`ACD` = first, `acd_b` = second) |
| `split_partial` | Composite `A/B` street — only one half resolved |
| `unmatched` | No row in [`ADRESSENOGD`](https://data.wien.gv.at/daten/geo?service=WFS&request=DescribeFeatureType&typeNames=ogdwien:ADRESSENOGD) matched |

*Note: this DE/EN toggle is complementary to the German narrative vignette at
[scrollytell\_de.html](scrollytell_de.html) — that page tells the story of
ACD codes; this page is a utility tool.*
:::

::: {data-lang="de"}
Diese Seite nutzt **nicht** die räumliche Verknüpfung oder die Gebäudegrundriss-Ebene
des Projekts. Es handelt sich um eine direkte Adresstabellen-Suche gegen
[`ogdwien:ADRESSENOGD`](https://data.wien.gv.at/daten/geo?service=WFS&request=DescribeFeatureType&typeNames=ogdwien:ADRESSENOGD)
(`r format(n_addresses, big.mark=".")` registrierte Adresspunkte), die vollständig in
[DuckDB-Wasm](https://duckdb.org/docs/api/wasm/overview.html) im Browser läuft.
Die räumliche Pipeline des Dashboards ist auf der [Methodik-Seite](methodology.qmd) beschrieben.

Die Verknüpfung verwendet drei normalisierte Schlüssel:

- **PLZ** — vierstellige Postleitzahl (als `VARCHAR`)
- **Straßenname** — `LOWER(TRIM(name_str))` mit der Benutzerspalte abgeglichen
- **Hausnummer** — `LOWER(TRIM(name_onr))` mit der Benutzerspalte abgeglichen

Schrebergarten-Adressen mit `/` im Straßennamen oder `Parz` in der Hausnummer
werden in zwei Suchversuche aufgeteilt (Fix B). Für Zeilen, bei denen die
Straße vorhanden ist, aber die exakte Hausnummer fehlt, wird die nächstgelegene
vorhandene Hausnummer herangezogen (Fix A).

### Was diese Seite nicht leistet

- ❌ Kein räumlicher Join via `R/join_buildings_zones.R`
- ❌ Kein `confidence_tier` (A–E, distanzbasiert)
- ❌ Kein `zone_id` oder `nearest_zone_dist_m`
- ❌ Kein Abgleich mit der `GEBAEUDEINFOOGD`-Gebäudegrundriss-Ebene

Die räumliche Anreicherung wird als Folgeaufgabe in
[Issue #42](https://github.com/JohnGavin/acd_area_climate_design/issues/42) verfolgt.

**Treffer-Qualität Legende:**

| Wert | Bedeutung |
|------|-----------|
| `exact` | Alle drei Schlüssel nach Normalisierung exakt übereinstimmend |
| `fuzzy_nearest_house` | PLZ + Straße stimmen überein; nächstgelegene vorhandene Hausnummer verwendet (Abstand in `house_distance`) |
| `split_both` | Zusammengesetzte `A/B`-Adresse — beide Hälften aufgelöst (`ACD` = erste, `acd_b` = zweite) |
| `split_partial` | Zusammengesetzte `A/B`-Adresse — nur eine Hälfte aufgelöst |
| `unmatched` | Keine Zeile in [`ADRESSENOGD`](https://data.wien.gv.at/daten/geo?service=WFS&request=DescribeFeatureType&typeNames=ogdwien:ADRESSENOGD) für diese Kombination gefunden |

*Hinweis: Der DE/EN-Umschalter ergänzt das deutsche Erzählvignette unter
[scrollytell\_de.html](scrollytell_de.html) — jene Seite erklärt ACD-Codes;
diese Seite ist ein Werkzeug.*
:::

### Performance

::: {data-lang="en"}
**Match rate on the user's 2,039-row test file (mostly Bezirke 21 + 22):**

| Algorithm | Matched | Rate |
|-----------|--------:|-----:|
| Baseline — exact join only (pre-#37) | 1,661 | 81.5% |
| **Fix A + Fix B (this page)** | **1,921** | **94.2%** |
| OGDAddressService REST API (external claim) | ~1,928 | ~94.5% |

Fix A (fuzzy nearest house) recovers 246 rows (12.1 pp). Fix B (composite
split) recovers 14 rows (0.7 pp). The residual 118 unmatched rows are
predominantly Schrebergarten parcel addresses and streets absent from
ADRESSENOGD.

All timings are for the DuckDB-WASM query phase after warm-up (first visit
adds ~3–4 s for DuckDB cold-start; subsequent queries on the same page load
are fast). The fuzzy fallback adds one extra query for unmatched rows only —
negligible when most rows match on the first pass.

| Rows | Operation | Estimated time |
|------|-----------|----------------|
| 12 (sample) | One DuckDB join | <100 ms after warm-up |
| 100 | One DuckDB join | <200 ms |
| 500 | One DuckDB join | <300 ms |
| 2,000 | Two DuckDB joins (exact + fuzzy pass) | ~600 ms |
| 10,000 | Two DuckDB joins + chunked CSV write | 1.5–2.5 s |
:::

Fix A (nächstgelegene Hausnummer) erholt 246 Zeilen (12,1 Pp.). Fix B

## Fix A — Fuzzy nearest house / Nächstgelegene Hausnummer

::: {.panel-tabset}

### Summary / Zusammenfassung

::: {data-lang="en"}
When `(PLZ, street_norm)` matches but the exact `house_norm` is absent from
ADRESSENOGD, the algorithm falls back to the nearest registered house number
on the same street. The numeric distance between the user's house number and
the nearest ADRESSENOGD house number is stored in the `house_distance` column
so users can filter low-confidence results. Distance is capped at 20 — rows
further than that remain `unmatched`.
:::

::: {data-lang="de"}
Wenn `(PLZ, Straßennorm)` übereinstimmt, die exakte Hausnummer aber nicht in
ADRESSENOGD enthalten ist, fällt der Algorithmus auf die nächstgelegene
registrierte Hausnummer in derselben Straße zurück. Die numerische Distanz
zwischen der eingegebenen und der gefundenen Hausnummer wird in der Spalte
`house_distance` gespeichert, damit unsichere Ergebnisse herausgefiltert
werden können. Abstände über 20 bleiben als `unmatched` erhalten.
:::

### Assumptions / Annahmen

::: {data-lang="en"}
- The nearest registered house number on the same street is a reasonable
  proxy for an unregistered parcel or new building.
- A numeric distance of ≤ 20 is close enough to be useful; beyond that the
  result is likely a different building entirely.
- The user's house number contains a leading integer (e.g. `21`, `21a`). If
  the house number is a parcel code like `Parz 38`, no leading integer is
  extracted and the fuzzy pass is skipped.
:::

::: {data-lang="de"}
- Die nächstgelegene registrierte Hausnummer in derselben Straße ist ein
  vertretbarer Ersatz für ein nicht registriertes Grundstück oder ein neues Gebäude.
- Ein numerischer Abstand von ≤ 20 ist nahe genug, um nützlich zu sein; darüber
  hinaus handelt es sich wahrscheinlich um ein anderes Gebäude.
- Die Hausnummer des Nutzers enthält eine führende Ganzzahl (z. B. `21`, `21a`).
  Ist die Hausnummer ein Parzellen-Code wie `Parz 38`, wird kein Wert extrahiert
  und der Fuzzy-Durchlauf übersprungen.
:::

### Benefits / Vorteile

::: {data-lang="en"}
- Recovers **246 rows (12.1 pp)** on the 2,039-row test file.
- Lifts overall match rate from **81.5% → ~93.6%** (Fix A alone).
- No external API calls — runs entirely in DuckDB-WASM in the browser.
- `house_distance` column lets the user decide whether to trust the result.
:::

::: {data-lang="de"}
- Erholt **246 Zeilen (12,1 Pp.)** auf der 2.039-zeiligen Testdatei.
- Hebt die Gesamttrefferquote von **81,5 % auf ~93,6 %** (nur Fix A).
- Keine externen API-Aufrufe — läuft vollständig in DuckDB-WASM im Browser.
- Die Spalte `house_distance` erlaubt es dem Nutzer, die Zuverlässigkeit
  selbst zu beurteilen.
:::

### Costs / Kosten

::: {data-lang="en"}
- Returns a **neighbour's ACD**, not necessarily the user's exact building.
  For buildings registered under a slightly different number (e.g. the city
  uses `21` while the user has `21a`), this is usually correct. For new
  construction on a vacant plot, the neighbour's ACD may be wrong.
- Adds a second DuckDB query for unmatched rows — adds ~100 ms on a 2,000-row
  file with ~18% unmatched rows.
- `house_distance` must be inspected manually to assess confidence.
:::

::: {data-lang="de"}
- Gibt die ACD eines **Nachbargebäudes** zurück, nicht zwingend die des
  gesuchten Gebäudes. Für Gebäude mit leicht abweichender Hausnummer (z. B.
  `21` statt `21a`) ist das meist korrekt. Bei Neubauten auf bisher unbebautem
  Grund kann die ACD eines Nachbarn falsch sein.
- Fügt bei nicht gefundenen Zeilen eine zweite DuckDB-Abfrage hinzu —
  ca. +100 ms bei 2.000 Zeilen mit ~18 % nicht gefundenen Adressen.
- `house_distance` muss manuell geprüft werden, um die Zuverlässigkeit
  einzuschätzen.
:::

### Works on / Funktioniert bei

::: {data-lang="en"}
- `1210, Achengasse, 21` — Achengasse 21 not in ADRESSENOGD; nearest is
  `Achengasse 19` (distance 2). ACD from `070268` block returned.
- `1210, Siemensstraße, 87` — if 87 is absent but 85 and 89 are present,
  distance 2, correct ACD returned.
- Any street where the odd/even side of the street has gaps in registered
  house numbers.
:::

::: {data-lang="de"}
- `1210, Achengasse, 21` — Achengasse 21 nicht in ADRESSENOGD; nächstgelegen
  ist `Achengasse 19` (Abstand 2). ACD aus dem Block `070268` wird zurückgegeben.
- `1210, Siemensstraße, 87` — wenn 87 fehlt, aber 85 und 89 vorhanden sind,
  Abstand 2, korrekte ACD.
- Jede Straße, bei der die gerade oder ungerade Seite Lücken in den
  registrierten Hausnummern hat.
:::

### Doesn't work on / Funktioniert nicht bei

::: {data-lang="en"}
- **Parcel codes** (`Parz 38`, `Parz 12b`) — no leading integer, fuzzy pass
  skipped; remains `unmatched`.
- **New buildings** not yet in ADRESSENOGD at all — the street is present but
  all house numbers are far from the user's. If the nearest is > 20 away,
  remains `unmatched`.
- **Streets genuinely absent** from ADRESSENOGD (35% of the unmatched cohort
  on the test file) — no candidate rows to compare against.
:::

::: {data-lang="de"}
- **Parzellen-Codes** (`Parz 38`, `Parz 12b`) — keine führende Ganzzahl,
  Fuzzy-Durchlauf übersprungen; bleibt `unmatched`.
- **Neubauten**, die noch nicht in ADRESSENOGD erfasst sind — Straße vorhanden,
  aber alle Hausnummern sind weit entfernt. Bei Abstand > 20 bleibt der Eintrag
  `unmatched`.
- **Straßen, die gar nicht in ADRESSENOGD** enthalten sind (35 % der nicht
  gefundenen Zeilen in der Testdatei) — keine Kandidaten für den Vergleich.
:::

:::

## Fix B — Composite-street splitter / Zusammengesetzte Straße

::: {.panel-tabset}

### Summary / Zusammenfassung

::: {data-lang="en"}
Some Vienna addresses identify corner parcels with two street names joined by
`/`, e.g. `Achengasse 4/Lavantgasse 1a`. The previous implementation claimed
to handle these but the split was not being applied before the main JOIN, so
no recovery occurred. Fix B reimplements the splitter in JavaScript *before*
the JOIN: each `A/B` street is expanded into two sub-rows, each looked up
independently. The results are aggregated as `acd_b` (second match) and
`match_quality = "split_both"` (both matched) or `"split_partial"` (one
matched).
:::

::: {data-lang="de"}
Manche Wiener Adressen bezeichnen Eckgrundstücke mit zwei durch `/`
verbundenen Straßennamen, z. B. `Achengasse 4/Lavantgasse 1a`. Die frühere
Implementierung behauptete, diese zu verarbeiten, aber die Aufteilung fand
vor dem JOIN nicht statt. Fix B reimplementiert den Splitter in JavaScript
*vor* dem JOIN: Jede `A/B`-Adresse wird in zwei Teilzeilen aufgeteilt, die
unabhängig voneinander nachgeschlagen werden. Die Ergebnisse werden als
`acd_b` (zweiter Treffer) und `match_quality = "split_both"` (beide gefunden)
oder `"split_partial"` (einer gefunden) zusammengeführt.
:::

### Assumptions / Annahmen

::: {data-lang="en"}
- A `/` in the street column indicates a composite address identifying the same
  physical location from two streets (corner building or shared driveway).
- A trailing number in each half of the split is the house number for that
  half, e.g. `Achengasse 4` → street `Achengasse`, house `4`.
- Both ACDs are valid for the same physical building; the user can choose
  either.
:::

::: {data-lang="de"}
- Ein `/` in der Straßenspalte bezeichnet eine zusammengesetzte Adresse, die
  denselben physischen Standort von zwei Straßen aus beschreibt (Eckgebäude
  oder gemeinsame Zufahrt).
- Eine abschließende Zahl in jeder Hälfte des Splits ist die Hausnummer für
  diese Hälfte, z. B. `Achengasse 4` → Straße `Achengasse`, Hausnummer `4`.
- Beide ACDs sind für dasselbe physische Gebäude gültig; der Nutzer kann
  eine davon wählen.
:::

### Benefits / Vorteile

::: {data-lang="en"}
- Recovers **14 rows (0.7 pp)** on the 2,039-row test file.
- Returns both ACDs when both halves resolve, giving the user the full
  picture for corner parcels.
- No distance estimation needed — the result is exact if the street+house
  exists in ADRESSENOGD.
:::

::: {data-lang="de"}
- Erholt **14 Zeilen (0,7 Pp.)** auf der 2.039-zeiligen Testdatei.
- Gibt beide ACDs zurück, wenn beide Hälften aufgelöst werden, und liefert
  dem Nutzer das vollständige Bild für Eckgrundstücke.
- Keine Abstandsschätzung erforderlich — das Ergebnis ist exakt, wenn
  Straße + Hausnummer in ADRESSENOGD vorhanden sind.
:::

### Costs / Kosten

::: {data-lang="en"}
- Returning two ACDs (`ACD` + `acd_b`) requires the user to inspect both
  columns for composite matches.
- Pure Schrebergarten parcel addresses like `Parz 38` remain unmatched even
  after the split because neither half maps to a registered building address.
- Expands input rows before the JOIN — minor overhead proportional to the
  number of composite rows in the upload file.
:::

::: {data-lang="de"}
- Die Rückgabe zweier ACDs (`ACD` + `acd_b`) erfordert, dass der Nutzer
  beide Spalten bei zusammengesetzten Treffern prüft.
- Reine Schrebergarten-Parzellenadressen wie `Parz 38` bleiben auch nach
  dem Split nicht gefunden, da keine Hälfte einer registrierten Gebäudeadresse
  entspricht.
- Eingabezeilen werden vor dem JOIN erweitert — geringer Mehraufwand
  proportional zur Anzahl der zusammengesetzten Zeilen.
:::

### Works on / Funktioniert bei

::: {data-lang="en"}
- `1210, Achengasse 4/Lavantgasse 1a, —` → ACD for `Achengasse 4` as `ACD`,
  ACD for `Lavantgasse 1a` as `acd_b`, `match_quality = "split_both"`.
- Corner buildings where both street addresses are registered in ADRESSENOGD.
- Any composite address where at least one half is a valid street+house
  combination in the reference data.
:::

::: {data-lang="de"}
- `1210, Achengasse 4/Lavantgasse 1a, —` → ACD für `Achengasse 4` als `ACD`,
  ACD für `Lavantgasse 1a` als `acd_b`, `match_quality = "split_both"`.
- Eckgebäude, bei denen beide Straßenadressen in ADRESSENOGD registriert sind.
- Jede zusammengesetzte Adresse, bei der mindestens eine Hälfte eine gültige
  Straße-Hausnummer-Kombination in den Referenzdaten ist.
:::

### Doesn't work on / Funktioniert nicht bei

::: {data-lang="en"}
- **Pure Schrebergarten parcels** like `Achengasse/Lavantgasse Parz 38` — the
  parcel number does not correspond to a registered building address in
  ADRESSENOGD; both halves miss.
- Composite strings where the separator has a different meaning (e.g.
  address range `1/3` meaning "houses 1 to 3" on a single street — these
  will be incorrectly split into two sub-lookups).
- Very long composite strings with 3+ parts — only the first two are attempted.
:::

::: {data-lang="de"}
- **Reine Schrebergarten-Parzellen** wie `Achengasse/Lavantgasse Parz 38` —
  die Parzellennummer entspricht keiner registrierten Gebäudeadresse in
  ADRESSENOGD; beide Hälften schlagen fehl.
- Zusammengesetzte Zeichenketten, bei denen das Trennzeichen eine andere
  Bedeutung hat (z. B. Adressbereich `1/3` für „Hausnummern 1 bis 3" auf
  einer einzelnen Straße — diese werden fälschlicherweise in zwei
  Teilabfragen aufgeteilt).
- Sehr lange zusammengesetzte Zeichenketten mit 3+ Teilen — nur die ersten
  beiden werden versucht.
:::

:::

## Fix C — REST API fallback (geplant / planned) {#fix-c}

::: {.panel-tabset}

### Summary / Zusammenfassung

::: {data-lang="en"}
**Status: PLANNED** — tracked in a separate issue. For rows still unmatched
after Fix A + Fix B, optionally call the city's
[`OGDAddressService.svc/GetAddressInfo`](https://data.wien.gv.at/daten/OGDAddressService.svc/GetAddressInfo)
REST endpoint per row. The API does its own fuzzy matching on the server side
and returns the canonical ACD. A concurrency cap of 8 parallel requests and a
maximum of ~250 calls per upload session keep the per-run cost manageable.
:::

::: {data-lang="de"}
**Status: GEPLANT** — wird in einem eigenen Issue verfolgt. Für nach Fix A + B
noch nicht gefundene Zeilen kann optional der städtische REST-Endpunkt
[`OGDAddressService.svc/GetAddressInfo`](https://data.wien.gv.at/daten/OGDAddressService.svc/GetAddressInfo)
pro Zeile aufgerufen werden. Die API führt serverseitig eigenes Fuzzy-Matching
durch und gibt die kanonische ACD zurück. Eine Parallelitäts-Obergrenze von
8 Anfragen und maximal ~250 Aufrufe pro Upload-Sitzung halten die Kosten
beherrschbar.
:::

### Assumptions / Annahmen

::: {data-lang="en"}
- The city's OGDAddressService API remains publicly available without
  authentication.
- ~200 ms per API call; 8 concurrent requests cap total time to ~6 s for 250
  residual rows.
- The API's own matching is more permissive than our static Parquet for
  Schrebergärten and edge-case spellings.
:::

::: {data-lang="de"}
- Der städtische OGDAddressService-Endpunkt bleibt ohne Authentifizierung
  öffentlich verfügbar.
- ~200 ms pro API-Aufruf; 8 parallele Anfragen begrenzen die Gesamtzeit auf
  ~6 s für 250 verbleibende Zeilen.
- Das eigene Matching der API ist für Schrebergärten und Sonderfälle
  großzügiger als unser statisches Parquet.
:::

### Benefits / Vorteile

::: {data-lang="en"}
- Expected to recover ~1–2 additional percentage points on top of Fix A + B.
- Canonicalises multi-unit ambiguity for the resolved rows.
- No local data updates needed — the API always reflects the current register.
:::

::: {data-lang="de"}
- Voraussichtlich ~1–2 weitere Prozentpunkte zusätzlich zu Fix A + B.
- Kanonisiert Mehrdeutigkeiten bei Mehrfamilienhäusern für die gefundenen Zeilen.
- Keine lokalen Datenaktualisierungen erforderlich — die API spiegelt immer
  den aktuellen Stand wider.
:::

### Costs / Kosten

::: {data-lang="en"}
- Requires network connectivity — not offline-capable for the fallback rows.
- City API may change or become unavailable without notice.
- User must consent to sending unmatched address fragments to an external server.
:::

::: {data-lang="de"}
- Erfordert Netzwerkzugang — für die Fallback-Zeilen nicht offline nutzbar.
- Die städtische API kann sich ohne Vorankündigung ändern oder ausfallen.
- Der Nutzer muss zustimmen, nicht gefundene Adressfragmente an einen
  externen Server zu senden.
:::

### Works on / Funktioniert bei

::: {data-lang="en"}
- Schrebergarten parcel addresses the API maps to a base building address.
- New buildings registered in the live Wien register but not yet in our
  Parquet snapshot.
:::

::: {data-lang="de"}
- Schrebergarten-Parzellenadressen, die die API einer Basisgebäudeadresse
  zuordnet.
- Neubauten, die im Live-Register Wien registriert sind, aber noch nicht in
  unserem Parquet-Snapshot enthalten sind.
:::

### Doesn't work on / Funktioniert nicht bei

::: {data-lang="en"}
- Addresses with no match in the live Wien register either.
- Offline use cases.
:::

::: {data-lang="de"}
- Adressen, die auch im Live-Register Wien keinen Treffer haben.
- Offline-Anwendungsfälle.
:::

:::

## Fix D — Multi-unit dedup (geplant / planned) {#fix-d}

::: {.panel-tabset}

### Summary / Zusammenfassung

::: {data-lang="en"}
**Status: PLANNED** — tracked in a separate issue. ADRESSENOGD contains
291,823 rows but only ~149,676 unique `(PLZ, street, house)` tuples. Around
13% of those tuples have more than one ACD — multi-unit buildings, separate
staircases, or sub-addresses. The current page deduplicates on `(PLZ, street,
house)` and returns one ACD arbitrarily. Fix D replaces the deduplication with
a `GROUP BY` returning all ACDs for a matched tuple, with a UI element
letting the user select or accept all.
:::

::: {data-lang="de"}
**Status: GEPLANT** — wird in einem eigenen Issue verfolgt. ADRESSENOGD
enthält 291.823 Zeilen, aber nur ~149.676 eindeutige `(PLZ, Straße, Haus)`-
Tupel. Etwa 13 % dieser Tupel haben mehr als eine ACD — Mehrfamilienhäuser,
separate Stiegen oder Unteradressen. Derzeit wird auf `(PLZ, Straße, Haus)`
dedupliziert und eine ACD willkürlich zurückgegeben. Fix D ersetzt die
Deduplizierung durch ein `GROUP BY`, das alle ACDs für ein gefundenes Tupel
zurückgibt, mit einem UI-Element, das dem Nutzer die Auswahl ermöglicht.
:::

### Assumptions / Annahmen

::: {data-lang="en"}
- The user knows their own unit / Stiege and can select from a list.
- Returning multiple ACDs is preferable to silently picking one at random.
:::

::: {data-lang="de"}
- Der Nutzer kennt seine eigene Einheit / Stiege und kann aus einer Liste
  auswählen.
- Mehrere ACDs zurückzugeben ist besser als eine zufällig auszuwählen.
:::

### Benefits / Vorteile

::: {data-lang="en"}
- Eliminates a hidden correctness bug affecting ~13% of matched rows.
- No extra queries needed — the information is already in ADRESSENOGD.
:::

::: {data-lang="de"}
- Beseitigt einen versteckten Korrektheitsfehler, der ~13 % der gefundenen
  Zeilen betrifft.
- Keine zusätzlichen Abfragen erforderlich — die Information ist bereits in
  ADRESSENOGD vorhanden.
:::

### Costs / Kosten

::: {data-lang="en"}
- Requires UI work to render and disambiguate multi-ACD cells.
- Download CSV format changes: multi-ACD rows need either multiple columns
  or a delimiter-separated value in the ACD column.
:::

::: {data-lang="de"}
- Erfordert UI-Arbeit zum Darstellen und Disambiguieren von Multi-ACD-Zellen.
- Das CSV-Download-Format ändert sich: Zeilen mit mehreren ACDs benötigen
  entweder mehrere Spalten oder einen trennzeichengetrennten Wert in der
  ACD-Spalte.
:::

### Works on / Funktioniert bei

::: {data-lang="en"}
- Any matched address in a multi-unit building — e.g. `Achengasse 4, 1210`
  with 82 registered ACDs returns all 82 for user selection.
:::

::: {data-lang="de"}
- Jede gefundene Adresse in einem Mehrfamilienhaus — z. B. `Achengasse 4,
  1210` mit 82 registrierten ACDs gibt alle 82 zur Nutzerauswahl zurück.
:::

### Doesn't work on / Funktioniert nicht bei

::: {data-lang="en"}
- Single-unit addresses — no change in behaviour (only one ACD anyway).
:::

::: {data-lang="de"}
- Einzeladressen — keine Verhaltensänderung (ohnehin nur eine ACD).
:::

:::

:::

```{=html}
<!-- ── duckdb-wasm + lookup JS ─────────────────────────────────────────────── -->

<!-- Inline Chart.js for the per-district bar chart (no server needed) -->
<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/chart.js@4.4.3/dist/chart.umd.min.js"></script>

<script type="module">
// ── NOTE ON SQL USAGE ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
// The `await conn.query("...")` calls below are duckdb-wasm's JS API.
// This is the idiomatic interface for duckdb-wasm; there is no JS equivalent
// of the R-side duckplyr package. The duckdplyr-not-sql rule applies to R code
// only. All R-side data access in this package uses duckplyr verbs.
// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

import * as duckdb from "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@duckdb/duckdb-wasm@1.29.0/+esm";

// ── Constants ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
const PARQUET_URL =
  "https://johngavin.github.io/acd_area_climate_design/data/addresses_2026-05-02.parquet";

// Max numeric house-number distance for fuzzy fallback (Fix A).
// Rows whose nearest house is further than this remain 'unmatched'.
const FUZZY_MAX_DISTANCE = 20;

// ── State ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
let parsedRows   = [];   // [{PLZ, Strasse, HausNr, ...original cols}]
let resultRows   = [];   // full result after JOIN
let colHeaders   = [];   // original column names from user file
let dbConn       = null; // duckdb-wasm connection (lazy init)
let dbReady      = false;

// ── Utility ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
function setProgress(pct, msg) {
  const sec = document.getElementById("progress-section");
  const bar = document.getElementById("progress-bar");
  const txt = document.getElementById("progress-msg");
  sec.style.display = pct < 100 ? "block" : "none";
  bar.style.width   = pct + "%";
  txt.textContent   = msg || "";
}

function escSql(s) {
  return String(s ?? "").replace(/'/g, "''");
}

// Extract the leading integer from a house-number string, e.g. "21a" → 21.
// Returns null if no integer found.
function extractLeadingInt(s) {
  const m = String(s ?? "").match(/^(\d+)/);
  return m ? parseInt(m[1], 10) : null;
}

// ── Fix B — Composite-street splitter ────────────────────────────────────
// For rows where Strasse contains "/" split into 1-2 sub-rows, each with
// composite_index and composite_total markers so mergeResults can identify
// which were from the same original row.
//
// "Achengasse 4/Lavantgasse 1a"  →  ["Achengasse 4", "Lavantgasse 1a"]
// Each side: attempt to pull a trailing number as the house number fallback.
function extractTrailingNumber(s) {
  const m = String(s ?? "").match(/(\d+\w*)$/);
  return m ? m[1] : null;
}

function splitComposite(rows, plzCol, streetCol, houseCol) {
  // Returns expanded array with extra fields:
  //   composite_index  — 0 for non-composite rows, 0/1/... for split parts
  //   composite_total  — 1 for non-composite, 2+ for split rows
  //   orig_idx         — index into original rows array
  //   PLZ, strasse_norm, hausnr_norm, garden_plot (same as before)
  const out = [];
  rows.forEach((r, idx) => {
    const plz    = String(r[plzCol]    ?? "").trim();
    const street = String(r[streetCol] ?? "").trim();
    const house  = String(r[houseCol]  ?? "").trim();
    const isParz = /parz/i.test(house);

    if (street.includes("/")) {
      const parts = street.split("/").map(s => s.trim()).filter(Boolean);
      parts.forEach((part, i) => {
        // If the part includes a trailing number use it as the house number
        const trailingNr = extractTrailingNumber(part);
        // Strip trailing number from street name to get clean street
        const streetOnly = part.replace(/\s*\d+\w*$/, "").trim();
        out.push({
          PLZ:              plz,
          strasse_norm:     streetOnly.toLowerCase(),
          hausnr_norm:      (trailingNr || house).toLowerCase(),
          garden_plot:      true,
          composite_index:  i,
          composite_total:  parts.length,
          orig_idx:         idx
        });
      });
    } else {
      out.push({
        PLZ:              plz,
        strasse_norm:     street.toLowerCase(),
        hausnr_norm:      house.toLowerCase(),
        garden_plot:      isParz,
        composite_index:  0,
        composite_total:  1,
        orig_idx:         idx
      });
    }
  });
  return out;
}

// ── DuckDB-Wasm init ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
async function initDuck() {
  if (dbReady) return;
  setProgress(5, "Loading DuckDB-Wasm…");
  const BUNDLES = duckdb.getJsDelivrBundles();
  const bundle  = await duckdb.selectBundle(BUNDLES);
  const worker  = await duckdb.createWorker(bundle.mainWorker);
  const logger  = new duckdb.ConsoleLogger();
  const db      = new duckdb.AsyncDuckDB(logger, worker);
  await db.instantiate(bundle.mainModule);
  dbConn  = await db.connect();

  setProgress(15, "Installing httpfs extension…");
  await dbConn.query("INSTALL httpfs; LOAD httpfs;");

  setProgress(25, "Registering address Parquet view…");
  await dbConn.query(`
    CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW addr AS
    SELECT *,
      LOWER(TRIM(NAME_STR))  AS street_norm,
      LOWER(TRIM(NAME_ONR))  AS house_norm,
      CAST(PLZ AS VARCHAR)   AS plz_norm
    FROM read_parquet('${PARQUET_URL}')
  `);
  dbReady = true;
  setProgress(35, "Address lookup ready.");
}

// ── Run the JOIN (exact pass) ──────────────────────────────────────────────
// Returns array of result objects, one per expanded row.
// Rows that didn't match have ACD = null and match_quality = 'unmatched'.
async function runExactLookup(expanded) {
  // Build VALUES list: include composite_index and composite_total
  const vals = expanded
    .map(r => `('${escSql(r.PLZ)}','${escSql(r.strasse_norm)}','${escSql(r.hausnr_norm)}',${r.garden_plot ? 1 : 0},${r.composite_index},${r.composite_total},${r.orig_idx})`)
    .join(",\n");

  setProgress(55, "Creating user input table…");
  await dbConn.query("DROP TABLE IF EXISTS user_in");
  await dbConn.query(`
    CREATE TABLE user_in (
      plz_in           VARCHAR,
      street_in        VARCHAR,
      house_in         VARCHAR,
      garden_plot      INTEGER,
      composite_index  INTEGER,
      composite_total  INTEGER,
      orig_idx         INTEGER
    )
  `);
  await dbConn.query(`INSERT INTO user_in VALUES ${vals}`);

  // Also add a row_id column for the fuzzy pass to reference
  await dbConn.query(`
    ALTER TABLE user_in ADD COLUMN row_id INTEGER DEFAULT 0
  `);
  await dbConn.query(`
    UPDATE user_in SET row_id = rowid
  `);

  setProgress(70, "Joining against ADRESSENOGD (exact pass)…");
  const res = await dbConn.query(`
    SELECT
      u.orig_idx,
      u.row_id,
      u.plz_in,
      u.street_in,
      u.house_in,
      u.garden_plot,
      u.composite_index,
      u.composite_total,
      a.ACD,
      a.SCD_NAME_STR       AS SCD,
      a.STRABS_ZUGANG_STR  AS STRABS,
      a.OBJEKT_ID,
      a.lon,
      a.lat,
      NULL::INTEGER        AS house_distance,
      CASE WHEN a.ACD IS NOT NULL THEN 'exact' ELSE 'unmatched' END AS match_quality
    FROM user_in u
    LEFT JOIN addr a
      ON u.plz_in    = a.plz_norm
     AND u.street_in = a.street_norm
     AND u.house_in  = a.house_norm
    ORDER BY u.orig_idx, u.composite_index
  `);

  return res.toArray().map(r => ({
    orig_idx:         Number(r.orig_idx),
    row_id:           Number(r.row_id),
    plz_in:           r.plz_in,
    street_in:        r.street_in,
    house_in:         r.house_in,
    garden_plot:      r.garden_plot === 1,
    composite_index:  Number(r.composite_index),
    composite_total:  Number(r.composite_total),
    ACD:              r.ACD,
    SCD:              r.SCD,
    STRABS:           r.STRABS,
    OBJEKT_ID:        r.OBJEKT_ID,
    lon:              r.lon,
    lat:              r.lat,
    house_distance:   null,
    match_quality:    r.match_quality
  }));
}

// ── Fix A — Fuzzy nearest-house fallback ──────────────────────────────────
// For rows that didn't match exactly, attempt to find the nearest house
// number on the same (PLZ, street_norm) combination.
// Only applies to non-composite rows where the street IS in ADRESSENOGD
// (i.e. the failure is a missing house number, not a missing street).
async function runFuzzyFallback(exactResults) {
  const unmatched = exactResults.filter(
    r => r.match_quality === "unmatched" && r.composite_total === 1
  );
  if (unmatched.length === 0) return exactResults;

  setProgress(75, "Fuzzy house-number fallback (Fix A)…");

  // Build VALUES for unmatched rows: (row_id, plz_in, street_in, house_in)
  const vals = unmatched
    .map(r => `(${r.row_id},'${escSql(r.plz_in)}','${escSql(r.street_in)}','${escSql(r.house_in)}')`)
    .join(",\n");

  await dbConn.query("DROP TABLE IF EXISTS unmatched_in");
  await dbConn.query(`
    CREATE TABLE unmatched_in (
      row_id    INTEGER,
      plz_in    VARCHAR,
      street_in VARCHAR,
      house_in  VARCHAR
    )
  `);
  await dbConn.query(`INSERT INTO unmatched_in VALUES ${vals}`);

  // Fuzzy query: for each unmatched row, find the nearest registered house
  // on the same (PLZ, street).  QUALIFY keeps only the single closest match.
  // DuckDB does not support QUALIFY with window functions in older builds —
  // use a subquery approach instead.
  const fuzzy = await dbConn.query(`
    WITH candidates AS (
      SELECT
        u.row_id,
        a.ACD,
        a.SCD_NAME_STR       AS SCD,
        a.STRABS_ZUGANG_STR  AS STRABS,
        a.OBJEKT_ID,
        a.lon,
        a.lat,
        ABS(
          COALESCE(TRY_CAST(REGEXP_EXTRACT(u.house_in,  '[0-9]+', 0) AS INTEGER), -9999) -
          COALESCE(TRY_CAST(REGEXP_EXTRACT(a.house_norm, '[0-9]+', 0) AS INTEGER), -9999)
        ) AS house_distance,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
          PARTITION BY u.row_id
          ORDER BY ABS(
            COALESCE(TRY_CAST(REGEXP_EXTRACT(u.house_in,  '[0-9]+', 0) AS INTEGER), -9999) -
            COALESCE(TRY_CAST(REGEXP_EXTRACT(a.house_norm, '[0-9]+', 0) AS INTEGER), -9999)
          )
        ) AS rn
      FROM unmatched_in u
      JOIN addr a ON u.plz_in = a.plz_norm AND u.street_in = a.street_norm
      WHERE a.house_norm REGEXP '^[0-9]'
        AND TRY_CAST(REGEXP_EXTRACT(u.house_in,  '[0-9]+', 0) AS INTEGER) IS NOT NULL
        AND TRY_CAST(REGEXP_EXTRACT(a.house_norm, '[0-9]+', 0) AS INTEGER) IS NOT NULL
    )
    SELECT * FROM candidates WHERE rn = 1
  `).catch(() => null);  // if the query fails (e.g. no REGEXP support), skip

  if (!fuzzy) return exactResults;

  // Index fuzzy results by row_id
  const fuzzyMap = {};
  fuzzy.toArray().forEach(r => {
    fuzzyMap[Number(r.row_id)] = {
      ACD:            r.ACD,
      SCD:            r.SCD,
      STRABS:         r.STRABS,
      OBJEKT_ID:      r.OBJEKT_ID,
      lon:            r.lon,
      lat:            r.lat,
      house_distance: Number(r.house_distance)
    };
  });

  // Patch the exactResults in-place: upgrade unmatched → fuzzy_nearest_house
  // only when the nearest house is within FUZZY_MAX_DISTANCE.
  return exactResults.map(r => {
    if (r.match_quality !== "unmatched" || r.composite_total !== 1) return r;
    const f = fuzzyMap[r.row_id];
    if (!f) return r;
    if (f.house_distance > FUZZY_MAX_DISTANCE) return r;
    return Object.assign({}, r, {
      ACD:            f.ACD,
      SCD:            f.SCD,
      STRABS:         f.STRABS,
      OBJEKT_ID:      f.OBJEKT_ID,
      lon:            f.lon,
      lat:            f.lat,
      house_distance: f.house_distance,
      match_quality:  "fuzzy_nearest_house"
    });
  });
}

// ── Combined lookup (exact + fuzzy) ───────────────────────────────────────
async function runLookup(expanded) {
  const exactResults = await runExactLookup(expanded);
  setProgress(80, "Fuzzy fallback pass…");
  return runFuzzyFallback(exactResults);
}

// ── Fix C — REST API fallback ──────────────────────────────────────────────
// Chunks an array into sub-arrays of at most `size` elements.
function chunks(arr, size) {
  const out = [];
  for (let i = 0; i < arr.length; i += size) out.push(arr.slice(i, i + size));
  return out;
}

// Session-level call budget (resets on page reload).
let restCallsUsed = 0;

async function restFallback(unmatchedRows, opts = {}) {
  const concurrency = opts.concurrency || 8;
  const maxCalls    = opts.maxCalls    || 250;
  const timeout     = opts.timeout     || 5000;
  const baseUrl     = "https://data.wien.gv.at/daten/OGDAddressService.svc/GetAddressInfo";

  const callsToMake = unmatchedRows.slice(0, maxCalls);
  const results     = [];
  const batches     = chunks(callsToMake, concurrency);
  let   done        = 0;

  for (const batch of batches) {
    const settled = await Promise.allSettled(batch.map(row => {
      const addr  = `${row.Strasse || row.__street__ || ""} ${row.HausNr || row.__house__ || ""}`.trim();
      const url   = `${baseUrl}?Address=${encodeURIComponent(addr)}&CRS=EPSG:4326`;
      const ctrl  = new AbortController();
      const timer = setTimeout(() => ctrl.abort(), timeout);
      return fetch(url, { signal: ctrl.signal })
        .then(r => {
          if (!r.ok) throw new Error(`HTTP ${r.status}`);
          return r.json();
        })
        .finally(() => clearTimeout(timer));
    }));

    settled.forEach((res, i) => {
      const row = batch[i];
      const f   = res.status === "fulfilled" && res.value?.features?.[0];
      if (f?.properties?.ACD) {
        results.push(Object.assign({}, row, {
          ACD:            f.properties.ACD,
          SCD:            f.properties.SCD       ?? "",
          STRABS:         f.properties.STRABS    ?? "",
          AdressID:       f.properties.AdressID  ?? "",
          lon:            f.geometry?.coordinates?.[0] ?? "",
          lat:            f.geometry?.coordinates?.[1] ?? "",
          match_quality:  "rest_api_fallback",
          rest_ranking:   f.properties.Ranking   ?? ""
        }));
      } else {
        results.push(Object.assign({}, row, { match_quality: "unmatched_after_rest" }));
      }
    });

    done += batch.length;
    restCallsUsed += batch.length;

    // Update progress UI
    const pct = Math.round(100 * done / callsToMake.length);
    const restMsg  = document.getElementById("rest-progress-msg");
    const restBar  = document.getElementById("rest-progress-bar");
    const restBudg = document.getElementById("rest-budget-display");
    if (restMsg)  restMsg.textContent  = `${done} / ${callsToMake.length} calls done…`;
    if (restBar)  restBar.style.width  = pct + "%";
    if (restBudg) restBudg.textContent =
      `${restCallsUsed} of ${maxCalls} max calls used this session`;
  }

  // Mark over-budget rows
  for (let i = maxCalls; i < unmatchedRows.length; i++) {
    results.push(Object.assign({}, unmatchedRows[i], { match_quality: "rest_skipped_over_budget" }));
  }

  return results;
}

// ── Merge results back to original rows ───────────────────────────────────
// Quality rank (lower = better):  exact=0, fuzzy=1, split_both=2,
// split_partial=3, rest_api_fallback=4, unmatched_after_rest=97,
// rest_skipped_over_budget=98, unmatched=99
const QUALITY_RANK = {
  exact:                     0,
  fuzzy_nearest_house:       1,
  split_both:                2,
  split_partial:             3,
  rest_api_fallback:         4,
  unmatched_after_rest:      97,
  rest_skipped_over_budget:  98,
  unmatched:                 99
};
function qualityRank(q) { return QUALITY_RANK[q] ?? 98; }

function mergeResults(origRows, expanded, joinedRows) {
  // Group expanded results by orig_idx
  const byOrig = {};
  joinedRows.forEach(r => {
    const k = r.orig_idx;
    if (!byOrig[k]) byOrig[k] = [];
    byOrig[k].push(r);
  });

  return origRows.map((row, idx) => {
    const parts = byOrig[idx] || [];
    if (parts.length === 0) {
      return Object.assign({}, row, {
        ACD: "", SCD: "", STRABS: "", OBJEKT_ID: "", lon: "", lat: "",
        house_distance: "", acd_b: "", match_quality: "unmatched"
      });
    }

    const compositeTotal = parts[0].composite_total;

    if (compositeTotal <= 1) {
      // Non-composite: just pick the best (should be one row)
      const best = parts.reduce((a, b) =>
        qualityRank(a.match_quality) <= qualityRank(b.match_quality) ? a : b
      );
      return Object.assign({}, row, {
        ACD:            best.ACD           ?? "",
        SCD:            best.SCD           ?? "",
        STRABS:         best.STRABS        ?? "",
        OBJEKT_ID:      best.OBJEKT_ID     ?? "",
        lon:            best.lon           ?? "",
        lat:            best.lat           ?? "",
        house_distance: best.house_distance ?? "",
        acd_b:          "",
        match_quality:  best.match_quality ?? "unmatched"
      });
    }

    // Composite row: parts[0] = first half, parts[1] = second half (if present)
    const p0 = parts.find(p => p.composite_index === 0);
    const p1 = parts.find(p => p.composite_index === 1);
    const m0 = p0 && p0.ACD ? true : false;
    const m1 = p1 && p1.ACD ? true : false;

    let matchQuality;
    if (m0 && m1)       matchQuality = "split_both";
    else if (m0 || m1)  matchQuality = "split_partial";
    else                matchQuality = "unmatched";

    const primary = m0 ? p0 : (m1 ? p1 : p0 || {});
    return Object.assign({}, row, {
      ACD:            primary.ACD           ?? "",
      SCD:            primary.SCD           ?? "",
      STRABS:         primary.STRABS        ?? "",
      OBJEKT_ID:      primary.OBJEKT_ID     ?? "",
      lon:            primary.lon           ?? "",
      lat:            primary.lat           ?? "",
      house_distance: "",
      acd_b:          (m1 && p1 ? p1.ACD : "") ?? "",
      match_quality:  matchQuality
    });
  });
}

// ── Match-rate chart ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
function renderChart(merged) {
  const byDistrict = {};
  merged.forEach(r => {
    const plz = r[Object.keys(r).find(k => k === "PLZ" || k === "_plz_")] ??
                r.__plzCol__ ?? r._plzVal_ ?? "";
    // Use plz_in if available (we stored it separately)
    const key = r.__plz__ || "";
    if (!byDistrict[key]) byDistrict[key] = { total: 0, matched: 0 };
    byDistrict[key].total++;
    if (r.match_quality !== "unmatched") byDistrict[key].matched++;
  });
  const labels = Object.keys(byDistrict).sort();
  const rates  = labels.map(k => {
    const d = byDistrict[k];
    return d.total > 0 ? Math.round(100 * d.matched / d.total) : 0;
  });

  const canvas = document.getElementById("district-chart");
  const existing = Chart.getChart(canvas);
  if (existing) existing.destroy();

  new Chart(canvas, {
    type: "bar",
    data: {
      labels,
      datasets: [{
        label: "Match rate (%)",
        data: rates,
        backgroundColor: "#0d6efd88",
        borderColor: "#0d6efd",
        borderWidth: 1
      }]
    },
    options: {
      responsive: true,
      plugins: {
        legend: { display: false },
        tooltip: { callbacks: { label: ctx => ctx.parsed.y + "%" } }
      },
      scales: {
        y: { min: 0, max: 100, ticks: { callback: v => v + "%" } }
      }
    }
  });
}

// ── HTML table (first 50 rows) ─────────────────────────────────────────────
function renderTable(merged) {
  const tbl  = document.getElementById("results-table");
  const cols = Object.keys(merged[0] || {}).filter(c => !c.startsWith("__"));
  const rows = merged.slice(0, 50);

  const head = `<thead><tr>${cols.map(c =>
    `<th style="border:1px solid #dee2e6; padding:4px 8px; background:#f8f9fa; white-space:nowrap;">${c}</th>`
  ).join("")}</tr></thead>`;

  const body = `<tbody>${rows.map(r =>
    `<tr>${cols.map(c => {
      const v   = r[c] ?? "";
      const isQ = c === "match_quality";
      const style = isQ && v === "exact"                     ? "background:#d1e7dd;" :
                    isQ && v === "fuzzy_nearest_house"      ? "background:#fff3cd;" :
                    isQ && v === "split_both"               ? "background:#cff4fc;" :
                    isQ && v === "split_partial"            ? "background:#e2e3e5;" :
                    isQ && v === "rest_api_fallback"        ? "background:#ffd9b3;" :
                    isQ && v === "unmatched_after_rest"     ? "background:#f8d7da;" :
                    isQ && v === "rest_skipped_over_budget" ? "background:#f0f0f0;" :
                    isQ && v === "unmatched"                ? "background:#f8d7da;" : "";
      return `<td style="border:1px solid #dee2e6; padding:4px 8px; ${style}">${v}</td>`;
    }).join("")}</tr>`
  ).join("")}</tbody>`;

  tbl.innerHTML = head + body;
}

// ── CSV download ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
function downloadCsv(merged) {
  const cols = Object.keys(merged[0] || {}).filter(c => !c.startsWith("__"));
  const header = cols.join(",");
  const body   = merged.map(r =>
    cols.map(c => {
      const v = String(r[c] ?? "");
      return v.includes(",") || v.includes('"') || v.includes("\n")
        ? `"${v.replace(/"/g, '""')}"` : v;
    }).join(",")
  ).join("\n");
  const csv  = header + "\n" + body;
  const blob = new Blob([csv], { type: "text/csv" });
  const url  = URL.createObjectURL(blob);
  const a    = document.createElement("a");
  a.href     = url;
  a.download = "addresses_with_acd.csv";
  document.body.appendChild(a);
  a.click();
  document.body.removeChild(a);
  setTimeout(() => URL.revokeObjectURL(url), 5000);
}

// ── File parsing ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
function autoDetect(cols) {
  const norm = c => c.toLowerCase().replace(/[^a-z]/g, "");
  const find = (keys) => cols.find(c => keys.includes(norm(c))) ?? cols[0];
  return {
    plz:    find(["plz", "postcode", "zip", "postleitzahl"]),
    street: find(["strasse", "street", "strase", "str", "streetname", "strassename", "name"]),
    house:  find(["hausnr", "hnr", "hausnummer", "nr", "housenumber", "number"])
  };
}

function populateSelects(cols, detected) {
  ["map-plz", "map-street", "map-hausnr"].forEach(id => {
    const sel = document.getElementById(id);
    sel.innerHTML = cols.map(c =>
      `<option value="${c}">${c}</option>`
    ).join("");
  });
  document.getElementById("map-plz").value    = detected.plz;
  document.getElementById("map-street").value = detected.street;
  document.getElementById("map-hausnr").value = detected.house;
}

async function parseFile(file) {
  const ext = file.name.split(".").pop().toLowerCase();
  if (ext === "csv") {
    return new Promise(resolve => {
      Papa.parse(file, {
        header: true,
        skipEmptyLines: true,
        complete: r => resolve({ rows: r.data, cols: r.meta.fields })
      });
    });
  } else {
    // xlsx
    const ab   = await file.arrayBuffer();
    const wb   = XLSX.read(ab, { type: "array" });
    const ws   = wb.Sheets[wb.SheetNames[0]];
    const rows = XLSX.utils.sheet_to_json(ws, { defval: "" });
    const cols = rows.length > 0 ? Object.keys(rows[0]) : [];
    return { rows, cols };
  }
}

// ── Match summary helper (used by both main run and REST update) ───────────
function updateMatchSummary(merged) {
  const nTotal        = merged.length;
  const nExact        = merged.filter(r => r.match_quality === "exact").length;
  const nFuzzy        = merged.filter(r => r.match_quality === "fuzzy_nearest_house").length;
  const nSplitBoth    = merged.filter(r => r.match_quality === "split_both").length;
  const nSplitPartial = merged.filter(r => r.match_quality === "split_partial").length;
  const nRestApi      = merged.filter(r => r.match_quality === "rest_api_fallback").length;
  const nAnyMatch     = nExact + nFuzzy + nSplitBoth + nSplitPartial + nRestApi;
  const nUnmatched    = nTotal - nAnyMatch;
  const pct           = nTotal > 0 ? Math.round(100 * nAnyMatch / nTotal) : 0;

  const lang = document.body.getAttribute("lang") || "en";
  const isDE = lang === "de";
  document.getElementById("match-summary").innerHTML =
    `<strong>${nAnyMatch.toLocaleString()}</strong> ` +
    (isDE ? "von" : "of") +
    ` <strong>${nTotal.toLocaleString()}</strong> ` +
    (isDE ? "Adressen zugeordnet" : "addresses matched") +
    ` (${pct}%). ` +
    `<span style="color:#198754;">&#10003; exact: ${nExact.toLocaleString()}</span>` +
    (nFuzzy        > 0 ? ` &nbsp; <span style="color:#fd7e14;">~ fuzzy: ${nFuzzy.toLocaleString()}</span>` : "") +
    (nSplitBoth    > 0 ? ` &nbsp; <span style="color:#0dcaf0;">&#8679; split (both): ${nSplitBoth.toLocaleString()}</span>` : "") +
    (nSplitPartial > 0 ? ` &nbsp; <span style="color:#6c757d;">&#8679; split (partial): ${nSplitPartial.toLocaleString()}</span>` : "") +
    (nRestApi      > 0 ? ` &nbsp; <span style="color:#fd7e14; font-weight:600;">&#127760; REST API: ${nRestApi.toLocaleString()}</span>` : "") +
    ` &nbsp; <span style="color:#dc3545;">&#10007; ` +
    (isDE ? "keine Übereinstimmung" : "unmatched") +
    `: ${nUnmatched.toLocaleString()}</span>`;
}

// ── Wire up UI ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
document.getElementById("drop-zone").addEventListener("click", () =>
  document.getElementById("file-input").click()
);

document.getElementById("drop-zone").addEventListener("dragover", e => {
  e.preventDefault();
  document.getElementById("drop-zone").style.background = "#e9ecef";
});

document.getElementById("drop-zone").addEventListener("dragleave", () => {
  document.getElementById("drop-zone").style.background = "#f8f9fa";
});

document.getElementById("drop-zone").addEventListener("drop", async e => {
  e.preventDefault();
  document.getElementById("drop-zone").style.background = "#f8f9fa";
  const file = e.dataTransfer.files[0];
  if (file) await handleFile(file);
});

document.getElementById("file-input").addEventListener("change", async e => {
  const file = e.target.files[0];
  if (file) await handleFile(file);
});

// "Try with sample" button: fetch the bundled xlsx and run it through the
// same handleFile() pipeline as a real upload would.
document.getElementById("try-sample-btn").addEventListener("click", async () => {
  setProgress(5, "Fetching sample file…");
  try {
    const resp = await fetch("../../data/sample_acd_test.xlsx");
    if (!resp.ok) throw new Error(`HTTP ${resp.status}`);
    const blob = await resp.blob();
    const file = new File([blob], "sample_acd_test.xlsx",
      { type: "application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet" });
    await handleFile(file);
  } catch (err) {
    setProgress(0, "Could not load sample: " + err.message);
  }
});

async function handleFile(file) {
  document.getElementById("file-name-display").textContent = file.name;
  document.getElementById("empty-state-msg").style.display = "none";
  setProgress(5, "Parsing file…");

  try {
    const { rows, cols } = await parseFile(file);
    parsedRows  = rows;
    colHeaders  = cols;
    const det   = autoDetect(cols);
    populateSelects(cols, det);
    document.getElementById("col-map-section").style.display = "block";
    setProgress(100, "");
  } catch (err) {
    setProgress(100, "");
    alert("Could not parse file: " + err.message);
  }
}

document.getElementById("run-btn").addEventListener("click", async () => {
  const plzCol    = document.getElementById("map-plz").value;
  const streetCol = document.getElementById("map-street").value;
  const houseCol  = document.getElementById("map-hausnr").value;

  document.getElementById("empty-state-msg").style.display = "none";
  document.getElementById("results-section").style.display = "none";

  try {
    await initDuck();

    setProgress(40, "Expanding rows (composite split + garden-plot detection)…");
    // Fix B: splitComposite replaces the old expandRows — handles "/" splits correctly
    const expanded = splitComposite(parsedRows, plzCol, streetCol, houseCol);

    // Fix A: runLookup now does exact pass + fuzzy fallback
    const joinedRows = await runLookup(expanded);

    // Tag each orig row with its PLZ for chart
    const withPlz = parsedRows.map((r, idx) => ({
      ...r,
      __plz__: String(r[plzCol] ?? "").trim()
    }));

    const merged = mergeResults(withPlz, expanded, joinedRows);

    resultRows = merged;

    const nTotal         = merged.length;
    const nExact         = merged.filter(r => r.match_quality === "exact").length;
    const nFuzzy         = merged.filter(r => r.match_quality === "fuzzy_nearest_house").length;
    const nSplitBoth     = merged.filter(r => r.match_quality === "split_both").length;
    const nSplitPartial  = merged.filter(r => r.match_quality === "split_partial").length;
    const nAnyMatch      = nExact + nFuzzy + nSplitBoth + nSplitPartial;
    const nUnmatched     = nTotal - nAnyMatch;
    const pct            = nTotal > 0 ? Math.round(100 * nAnyMatch / nTotal) : 0;

    updateMatchSummary(merged);

    renderChart(merged);
    renderTable(merged);

    document.getElementById("results-section").style.display = "block";
    setProgress(100, "");

    // Show REST fallback button if there are unmatched rows
    const restSec = document.getElementById("rest-fallback-section");
    if (nUnmatched > 0) {
      const el1 = document.getElementById("rest-unmatched-count");
      const el2 = document.getElementById("rest-unmatched-count-de");
      if (el1) el1.textContent = nUnmatched.toLocaleString();
      if (el2) el2.textContent = nUnmatched.toLocaleString();
      const restBudg = document.getElementById("rest-budget-display");
      if (restBudg) restBudg.textContent =
        `${restCallsUsed} of 250 max calls used this session`;
      restSec.style.display = "block";
    } else {
      restSec.style.display = "none";
    }
  } catch (err) {
    setProgress(100, "");
    console.error(err);
    alert("Lookup failed: " + err.message +
          "\n\nCheck the browser console for details.");
  }
});

document.getElementById("download-btn").addEventListener("click", () => {
  if (resultRows.length > 0) downloadCsv(resultRows);
});

// ── Fix C — REST API fallback button ──────────────────────────────────────
document.getElementById("rest-btn").addEventListener("click", async () => {
  const btn = document.getElementById("rest-btn");
  btn.disabled = true;

  const lang = document.body.getAttribute("lang") || "en";
  const isDE = lang === "de";

  // Identify rows still unmatched (only true 'unmatched' rows; skip composites)
  // We need to supply street/house from the original columns.
  // resultRows carry the original user columns plus ACD/match_quality additions.
  const plzCol    = document.getElementById("map-plz").value;
  const streetCol = document.getElementById("map-street").value;
  const houseCol  = document.getElementById("map-hausnr").value;

  const unmatched = resultRows.filter(r =>
    r.match_quality === "unmatched"
  ).map(r => Object.assign({}, r, {
    // Provide normalised aliases the restFallback function can read
    Strasse: String(r[streetCol] ?? "").trim(),
    HausNr:  String(r[houseCol]  ?? "").trim()
  }));

  if (unmatched.length === 0) {
    btn.disabled = false;
    return;
  }

  const progressWrap = document.getElementById("rest-progress-wrap");
  const restBar      = document.getElementById("rest-progress-bar");
  const restMsg      = document.getElementById("rest-progress-msg");
  progressWrap.style.display = "block";
  restBar.style.width        = "0%";
  restMsg.textContent        =
    isDE ? "REST API wird aufgerufen…" : "Calling REST API…";

  try {
    const apiResults = await restFallback(unmatched, {
      concurrency: 8,
      maxCalls:    250,
      timeout:     5000
    });

    // Merge apiResults back into resultRows by object identity (ref comparison
    // won't work after map), so use a positional index map via a WeakMap.
    // Strategy: apiResults items carry the same PLZ/street/house keys; build
    // a lookup keyed by the row's position in the unmatched list and splice
    // back using the row index stored in __restIdx__.
    const apiByIdx = {};
    apiResults.forEach((r, i) => { apiByIdx[i] = r; });

    // Rebuild resultRows: replace unmatched rows with their API results
    let apiCursor = 0;
    resultRows = resultRows.map(r => {
      if (r.match_quality !== "unmatched") return r;
      const updated = apiByIdx[apiCursor++];
      return updated ?? r;
    });

    updateMatchSummary(resultRows);
    renderChart(resultRows);
    renderTable(resultRows);

    // Update or hide the REST section
    const nStillUnmatched = resultRows.filter(
      r => r.match_quality === "unmatched" ||
           r.match_quality === "unmatched_after_rest"
    ).length;
    const el1 = document.getElementById("rest-unmatched-count");
    const el2 = document.getElementById("rest-unmatched-count-de");
    if (el1) el1.textContent = nStillUnmatched.toLocaleString();
    if (el2) el2.textContent = nStillUnmatched.toLocaleString();

    const restBudg = document.getElementById("rest-budget-display");
    if (restBudg) restBudg.textContent =
      `${restCallsUsed} of 250 max calls used this session`;

    restMsg.textContent = isDE
      ? `Fertig — ${apiResults.filter(r => r.match_quality === "rest_api_fallback").length} zusätzliche Treffer via REST API`
      : `Done — ${apiResults.filter(r => r.match_quality === "rest_api_fallback").length} additional matches via REST API`;

    progressWrap.style.display = "block";
    // Disable button to avoid double-calling
    btn.textContent = isDE ? "✓ REST API abgeschlossen" : "✓ REST API done";

  } catch (err) {
    restMsg.textContent = (isDE ? "Fehler: " : "Error: ") + err.message;
    btn.disabled = false;
  }
});
</script>
```
